text:
Recent work supports aligning item text with behavioral representations, but evidence is mostly based on pretrained language models. [CLA-Rec (ICDM 2024)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10884256/) contrastively aligns description embeddings with collaborative information; [CALRec (RecSys 2024)](https://research.google/pubs/calrec-contrastive-alignment-of-generative-llms-for-sequential-recommendation/) reports benefits from contrastive user/item alignment using PaLM-2. These results motivate auxiliary alignment, but do not establish gains for corpus-only text encoders trained from scratch, sparse items specifically, or NextItNet. No directly matching NextItNet study surfaced in this search.

Semantic hard negatives require caution: similar descriptions can identify plausible alternatives rather than genuine negatives. [SID4SRec (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0950705126010221) explicitly filters semantically overlapping negatives and reports improvements on sparse Amazon benchmarks, although it uses unavailable category/brand attributes. [KGSCL (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S089360802500070X) preserves augmentation semantics through explicit substitution/complementary relationships; title similarity alone cannot supply that evidence. Neither establishes that text implies compatibility or purchase need.

A constraint-compatible hypothesis—not a literature-validated recipe—is a small, randomly initialized token encoder over supplied titles/descriptions, jointly trained with NextItNet using a weak item-ID/text alignment loss and the existing next-item objective. Shared tokens could transfer supervision to infrequent items; benefit remains uncertain with limited corpus data. Compare alignment alone against a modest mixture of random and text-similar training negatives, excluding known training positives and duplicate item IDs. Retain one jointly trained network, checkpoint, and neural score per category; select using the fixed macro validation HR@10.
